name: top-bar
title: Top bar
description: The app bar of a phone-first screen: a back button, a title that truncates properly, trailing actions and a large title that settles on scroll.
docs: Put the bar inside the element that scrolls, as its first child: with sticky (the default) it stays at the top, and the nearest scrolling parent is found by itself (scrollContainer takes a ref when it is another element). title is the name of the screen and subtitle a lighter line under it. onBack shows a back button, a chevron named by backLabel ('Back to orders'; 'Back' by default), and backHref makes it a link that onBack still handles on a plain click; leading replaces it with your own element. actions is a list of { id, label, icon, onSelect, href, disabled, destructive, priority, pinned } shown as icon buttons named by their label. The bar measures itself: when the back button, the whole title and the actions no longer fit, the actions fold into a 'More actions' menu before the title is cut, the lowest priority first (equal priorities from the end), pinned ones never; only when even the menu button leaves too little room does the title truncate with an ellipsis, and its full text stays in the page for assistive technology. large adds a big title under the bar that scrolls away with the content; as it goes under the bar the bar's own title fades in, the progress being read from where the big title is, not from a number you pass. The title is always the one heading: the large one when there is one (the bar's copy is then hidden from assistive technology) and the bar's own otherwise, so the outline never doubles; as sets its level, h1 by default, so pass h2 or lower on a page that has its own h1. The bar adds the top safe-area inset (env(safe-area-inset-top), or the CSS variable --top-bar-inset when that is larger, for a frame that draws its own notch). A sticky bar has a bottom border only once content has scrolled under it (once the large title has gone, when there is one); a bar that is not sticky always has one; borderless removes it. labels holds the two hidden names for another language.
